articleTitle: A European survey of public networks management systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management and Signalling
abstract: Gives an overview of today's TMN (telecommunication management network) systems in the public networks environment in Europe. A set of relevant 'network types' and 'management functions' have been identified. In regard to today's physical implementation of the management functions, the main distinction was whether those functions are incorporated in network equipment (e.g. exchange systems), or support systems (e.g. O&M centers). This distinction was based either on the criteria of either physical or logical separation (e.g. separate software systems with a common hardware support). The SSs were further categorized into a hierarchical structure. Description of existing implementation has identified the relevant 'management functions' for each 'network type'. In addition, the collected data have been analyzed on a functional basis in order to give a Pan European overview of the current situation. The results cover 13 PTOs operations of 61 public networks, involving a total of 266 types of management equipment performing TMN functions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management and Signalling
abstract: British Telecom's Open Network Architecture for Management (ONA-M) is part of the company's overall approach to information systems. It's objective is to develop a consistent approach to the analysis and modelling of communications systems management with an initial focus on models to permit interoperability between the management systems of a number of BT products and services including: Private Circuit Services, Private Network Products, and between internal management systems used for the BT network. The philosophy adopted has been to start with a business oriented analysis of the requirements, and to apply an OSI and OSI management standards based approach to the solution, using OSI/NM forum technical agreements where appropriate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management and Signalling
abstract: The major driver for the deployment of SDH technology in transport networks around the world is the benefit associated with progressive automation of network management. The target network will consist of functionally integrated network elements, combining the functionalities of many layers and perspectives interconnected by high capacity optical fibres. The nature of the client/server relationship between network layers is summarised. The CCITT are developing standards to support the deployment of automated management procedures in SDH networks. The standards for the transmission management network itself come within the TMN activity of SGIV while the standards for the transport network architecture including management features come within the SGXVIII activity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital subscriber signalling for network management
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management and Signalling
abstract: Examines the issues involved in the support of network management functions at the ISDN user-network interface. The structure of the ISDN user-network interface is reviewed and some key areas in the relation of ISDN to the TMN (telecommunication management network) are noted. The major areas considered are requirements for the digital subscriber signalling system used at the ISDN user-network interface and the evolution of an architecture and protocols to support them.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management and Signalling
abstract: In today's digital network, software-based telephony services are undertaken by stored-program control logic and data embedded in digital switching systems. The cost/performance trends in processing technology encourage greater distribution of intelligence, thus creating opportunities for increased flexibility and modularity of service provision. This has led to development of the intelligent network (IN) architecture. The key technical objectives of IN in addressing the needs of the customer are: rapid and flexible introduction of new services; increased control of service definitions, costs, timescales; stable and standardized interfaces.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management and Signalling
abstract: Aspects of the paper relate particularly to the applicability of TMN concepts to the network management requirements of the Integrated Broadband Communications Network (IBCN) proposed by RACE. The IBCN is a proposed pan-European broadband multi-service network. The network management requirements of IBCN are, in general, extensions and extrapolations of the requirements of existing networks and therefore serve well to illustrate the trends in requirements for future telecommunications systems. The paper contains an introduction to network management requirements, TMN concepts and RACE extensions to TMN concepts, followed by discussion of some issues facing implementers of a TMN.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management and Signalling
abstract: Discusses the network size and geographic coverage, network technology, national network interconnection, growth rates, signalling scenarios, international service, national network structures, and network management.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management and Signalling
abstract: The CCITT No.7 O,A&M User Part (OMAP) is defined in CCITT Recommendation Q.795. The latest version will appear in the CCITT Blue Book. OMAP is still evolving. OMAP is responsible for managing the SS No.7 network-ultimately is might be absorbed into TMN, or perhaps a better solution would be to provide an interface above OSI layer 7, at the process level, for TMN to control OMAP.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management and Signalling
abstract: The paper draws attention to the ways in which the introduction of competition in the provision of telecommunication systems and services in the United Kingdom is likely to affect the management, both individually and collectively, of the various networks used to support those services. Attention is drawn to some of the basic principles of interconnection in order to expose the network management implications for provision, operation and maintenance of systems. It is hoped that the paper will form a useful input to the studies of standards for telecommunication management networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management and Signalling
abstract: Much impetus has been given to network management standardization by the formation of the OSI/Network Management Forum, an organisation whose sole focus is on network management. The approach adopted is pragmatic and concentrates at first on linking the many 'islands' of network management created by the lack of standards, in order to allow them, at last, to communicate with each other. This has been done by adopting a simple dumb-bell architecture which can be interpreted, in the first instance, as enabling peer-to-peer communication between network management centres. This architecture is not restricted solely to peer-to-peer communication.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
